title: Security gates must fail-safe: block when unable to evaluate, always run graph-wide checks
context: Multi-agent audit found four independent paths where enforcement gates silently passed despite being unable to evaluate constraints (fail-open). Each is dangerous: blocking rules that cannot verify default to allowed instead of blocked.
decision: Rebuilt gate logic so (1) zero-file diffs still run conformance checks; (2) all file types feed scope rules, not code-only; (3) all matching forbids checked, not first-match-wins; (4) external packages resolve from edges, not just symbols; (5) all gates always run regardless of diff size
consequences: Delete-only PRs no longer skip conformance gates; deletions of guarded symbols now caught
Scope rules apply to config/workflow files, not just code
Dependency forbid rules check every matching specifier; shadowing by unrelated file order no longer masks violations
External package constraints (`not-imports X <pkg>`) now enforce instead of trivially passing
alternatives_rejected: Warn-only mode instead of blocking: would still allow unsafe code through on audit fatigue
Special-case each gate: loses the general principle that gates should run regardless of diff shape
Scope rules to code-only: rules often apply to infrastructure files (.github/workflows, package.json, etc.)
